before.title: CAALM: UCD-PDL1 immunotherapy for oral melanoma metastatic to lung
before.center: UC Davis Veterinary Center for Clinical Trials
before.funding: 🟢 Study-supported. UCD-PDL1 treatments, required diagnostics and imaging, and management of study-related adverse events up to $2,000 are covered; owners pay pre-enrollment consultation and eligibility diagnostics.

before.title: COTC033 repurposing vaccine immunity to treat canine cancers
before.center: Colorado State University Flint Animal Cancer Center
before.status: Actively recruiting — listed on CSU current clinical trials page
before.contacts: CSU Clinical Trials — csuoncologytrials@colostate.edu · 970-297-4001; Missouri Oncology Clinical Trials — cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu · 573-882-7821
before.funding: 🟢 Study-funded care at both confirmed sites. CSU covers protocol screening, study examinations, blood/urine tests, imaging, biopsies and vaccine treatments, and provides a $3,000 CSU veterinary-hospital account credit toward additional treatment when the dog completes or leaves the study. Missouri covers protocol treatment, rechecks, initial staging and treatment of adverse effects, and provides a $1,000 gift toward additional cancer treatment after completion. Owners remain responsible for original diagnosis and care outside the study.
before.notes: COTC033 is one multicenter protocol, not separate CSU and Missouri trials. Published eligibility includes a biopsy- or cytology-confirmed 2–8 cm solid tumor and body weight 15–60 kg. Missouri excludes mast cell tumor, cutaneous hemangiosarcoma, thyroid carcinoma and lymphoma; prior experimental therapy is not allowed, and washouts apply for chemotherapy/radiation, immunomodulators and corticosteroids.

before.title: FAP CAR-T cell therapy for canine soft tissue sarcoma
before.center: Tufts Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine
before.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on the institution’s current clinical-trials page
before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. The study covers FAP CAR-T cancer treatment through Day 56, provides $2,000 toward tumor removal, and covers treatment of side effects related to biopsy, cyclophosphamide and FAP CAR-T administration; unrelated care is owner-paid.
before.notes: Dogs need a 2-8 cm soft tissue sarcoma, resectable or non-resectable, adequate CBC/chemistry/urinalysis and no incompatible major heart, liver or kidney disease. Untreated tumors and recurrent tumors after chemotherapy and/or radiation may qualify; chemotherapy must have ended at least 14 days before enrollment. Excludes metastatic disease predicting survival under three months, concurrent experimental cancer therapy, pregnancy/lactation, autoimmune disease other than atopic dermatitis, prior monoclonal checkpoint inhibitor such as gilvetmab, or personalized T-cell vaccine/immunotherapy.

after.title: Intratumoral cowpea mosaic virus immunotherapy for canine solid tumors
after.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
after.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page

after.funding: 🟢 Study-subsidized. The protocol brochure states that owners pay only for diagnostics, imaging, palliative care and other tests or care needed outside the study.
after.notes: The current Study 1 brochure explicitly includes mammary tumors alongside melanomas, soft tissue sarcomas, mast cell tumors and thyroid tumors. CPMV is injected weekly for one month before response evaluation; an additional month or subsequent therapy may be considered by the clinician. Off-study diagnostics, imaging and palliative care are owner-paid. Required on-study follow-up lasts at least three months.
after.special_requirement: Confirmed active melanoma, soft tissue sarcoma, mast cell tumor, thyroid tumor or mammary tumor accessible for intratumoral injection. No other chemotherapy or immunotherapy concurrently with CPMV; anesthesia and severe chronic disease risks require VROC screening.

after.title: CAR-Neutrophils Combined with Radiation for Canine Glioma
after.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on UT Southwestern VROC current trials page
after.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
after.notes: Current Study 6 combines radiation with CAR-neutrophils in dogs with glioma. Assignment may include radiation alone or weekly/monthly immunotherapy; not every arm receives CAR-neutrophils. CT precedes radiation and at least two MRIs are required. Severe chronic/anesthesia-risk disease is excluded; post-treatment follow-up is at least three months. The generic canine/feline brochure heading does not establish a feline cohort.
after.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
after.funding: 🟢 Study-subsidized. The protocol brochure states that owners pay only for diagnostics, imaging, palliative care and other tests or care needed outside the study.
after.special_requirement: Primary/recurrent glioma; other brain tumor eligibility must be confirmed by VROC. Prednisone must be feasible with a six-week taper. Prior radiation for the current cancer excludes enrollment. Other chemotherapy/immunotherapy must stop or undergo a team-defined washout; antioxidant supplements must be stoppable.

after.title: Intratumoral vs IV Carboplatin with or without HIFU for Canine Melanoma
after.intervention: Intratumoral nanoparticle/microparticle carboplatin versus IV carboplatin with or without HIFU
after.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
after.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
after.funding: ⚪ Owner-paid. The protocol brochure states that owners fully pay for the study, although possible subsidies may be available.
after.special_requirement: Confirmed active melanoma with a tumor accessible for intratumoral injection and/or ultrasound. Prior chemotherapy excludes participation. after.notes: Current Study 4 uses IV or intratumoral carboplatin, with or without HIFU, every three weeks for 3–4 cycles. Follow-up is required for at least three months. All treatment is owner-paid, with only possible subsidies. The protocol is canine despite the generic canine/feline brochure heading.

after.title: Compassionate-Use Protocol for Advanced Non-Resectable Tumors
after.intervention: Investigational therapy, chemotherapy, immunotherapy and combination approaches under a prospective compassionate-use protocol
after.center: UT Southwestern Veterinary Research and Oncology Clinic
after.contacts: Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator — 214-645-6221; VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu
after.funding: ⚪ Owner-paid. The protocol brochure states that owners fully pay for the study, although possible subsidies may be available.
after.notes: Current Study 5 is canine despite the generic canine/feline heading. Examples include urothelial carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma and meningioma. Options can include chemotherapy, radiation, HIFU and immunotherapy, individually chosen after clinician/research-board review. Owners fully pay, with only possible subsidies; no free-care claim. At least one month of follow-up is required.
after.special_requirement: Advanced, inoperable or recurrent solid tumor not covered by another VROC study; expected survival must exceed three weeks and weight must exceed 2.5 kg. Owner must decline surgery or standard-of-care therapy; organ function, anesthesia risks and individualized treatment require clinician/research-board review.

before.title: Whole-abdomen radiation therapy for relapsed feline small-cell gastrointestinal lymphoma
before.center: Texas A&M School of Veterinary Medicine
before.funding: 🟡 Study-related costs are covered after enrollment. Owners pay screening blood/urine panels within 14 days before enrollment; overnight hospital housing may incur an additional charge.
before.notes: Current investigator-linked primary protocol: biopsy-confirmed feline small-cell gastrointestinal lymphoma, either newly diagnosed but difficult to medicate or relapsed after chemotherapy. Cats need pretreatment blood/urine testing within 14 days and at least seven days without chemotherapy or corticosteroids before radiation. Owners must live within a six-hour drive of College Station. Whole-abdomen radiation under anesthesia on days 0-4, then visits at two and six weeks; owner stool samples and quality-of-life surveys through up to 18 months. Study-related costs after enrollment are covered; screening panels and possible overnight hospital housing remain owner costs.
